title: HyPAS: A Hybrid Optimization Framework for Placement and Sizing Co-Optimization
evidence_span: HyPAS alternates discrete signoff optimization in OpenROAD with differentiable DREAMPlace refinement, using a GNN timing-power surrogate and a straight-through estimator to bridge continuous gradients and discrete library parameters; the official description reports superior PPA gains with competitive runtime against ICCAD 2025 contest results and state-of-the-art methods, without numeric values.
problem: Incremental placement, sizing, and buffering flows use isolated heuristic stages and timing analyses, while differentiable placement can be fragile near legality and timing-closure boundaries.
method_or_artifact: Hybrid discrete/differentiable placement and sizing, OpenROAD signoff legality/repair, DREAMPlace gradients, GNN timing-power surrogate, and straight-through estimator.
workload_or_benchmark: Physical-design placement and gate-sizing benchmarks compared with ICCAD 2025 CAD Contest and state-of-the-art methods; designs, process node, and PPA metrics are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Standard-cell placement, timing closure, buffering, and library parameters; OpenROAD/DREAMPlace tooling, process, and signoff extraction are unspecified.
limits: No PPA values, design sizes, timing constraints, runtime, surrogate error, or contest configurations are supplied.
Differentiable surrogates and signoff repair may behave differently across libraries and process nodes.
Official description only; physical-design validity requires paper-level verification.

title: Exploiting Dependency and Parallelism: Real-Time Scheduling and Analysis for GPU Tasks
evidence_span: The method represents GPU tasks as DAGs, scales kernel-level parallelism, and establishes inter-kernel dependencies to reduce a predictable response-time bound without kernel-priority assumptions; a CUDA implementation on synthetic and real-world benchmarks reports up to 32.8% lower worst-case makespan and 21.3% lower measured task execution time.
problem: GPU kernel dependencies and resource contention create unpredictable delays for safety-critical real-time applications.
method_or_artifact: DAG-based GPU scheduler and safe, non-pessimistic makespan analysis implemented through standard CUDA APIs.
workload_or_benchmark: Synthetic and real-world DAG-structured GPU tasks; GPU model, task graphs, utilization, timing constraints, and baseline methods are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: CUDA-capable GPU with no additional hardware/software support; kernel preemption, streams, memory transfers, and driver version are unspecified.
baselines: existing GPU real-time scheduling and analysis methods
metrics: Up to 21.3% lower measured execution time
limits: The description omits graph sizes, utilization, timing deadlines, GPU/driver settings, and baseline tuning.
Measured execution time and safe makespan bounds are distinct metrics with different assumptions.
Official description only; schedulability and safety claims require paper-level verification.

title: Safe-IoT: A Memory-Efficient HW/SW Co-Designed ML-DSA Accelerator for IoT Edge Devices
evidence_span: Safe-IoT combines a memory-efficient IoT-oriented NTT circuit with a low-cost LUT-based modular multiplier in a hardware/software co-designed ML-DSA accelerator; the official description reports up to 3.0x throughput over CPU designs, 2.6–8.3x lower on-chip RAM than similar co-designs, and 4.28–176.53x area-time-product improvement.
problem: IoT devices need secure post-quantum signatures but CPU implementations are slow and fixed hardware accelerators can be memory-heavy and difficult to adapt.
method_or_artifact: Memory-efficient ML-DSA accelerator with MI-NTT circuit, LUT modular multiplication, and hardware/software co-design.
workload_or_benchmark: ML-DSA post-quantum signature operations on IoT edge devices; parameter set, message sizes, CPU baseline, process, and software stack are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: IoT-oriented accelerator with on-chip RAM and NTT/modular arithmetic; process node, frequency, area, power, and memory technology are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 3.0x throughput improvement over CPU
limits: The description omits ML-DSA parameter set, timing/area/power, security leakage model, CPU identity, and RAM accounting.
Large ATP ranges may reflect different parameter sets and comparison boundaries.
Official description only; cryptographic correctness and hardware security require paper-level verification.

title: Vten: Tensor-Centric Verification Framework for Domain-Specific Accelerators
evidence_span: vTen decouples verification intent from execution mechanics through a declarative tensor-centric DSL and kernel-granular batching, reducing host-simulator interaction; on a production-scale 3D U-Net accelerator the official description reports 2x lower simulation latency and 60.3% lower code complexity than Cocotb.
problem: Tensor-centric software models and signal-level hardware testbenches create a semantic gap, while fine-grained UVM/Cocotb interaction imposes synchronization overhead.
method_or_artifact: Declarative tensor-centric verification DSL with kernel-granular batching and decoupled execution.
workload_or_benchmark: Production-scale 3D U-Net domain-specific accelerator; testbench size, simulator, coverage, correctness criteria, and UVM baseline are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Domain-specific accelerator simulation with host/simulator interaction; RTL language, simulator, hardware scale, and test environment are unspecified.
limits: The description omits test coverage, simulator settings, latency measurement, code-complexity definition, and baseline implementation.
Batching can improve throughput while changing debug granularity and failure localization.
Official description only; verification completeness and usability require paper-level verification.

title: Adaptive Read Retry Table Extension for Enhanced Data Reliability in 3D NAND Flash Memory
evidence_span: The Adaptive RRT Extension framework combines wordline-aware interpolated retry and multi-dimensional guided retry to avoid read-retry-parameter burnout in retained 3D NAND; the official description reports recovery of up to 99% of failed pages and preservation of up to 99% and 84% usable capacity after 12- and 30-month retention, versus a baseline retaining 90% or reaching end-of-life.
problem: Charge leakage during retention exhausts fixed read-retry voltage combinations, making pages undecodable and degrading NAND capacity and lifetime.
method_or_artifact: Adaptive read-retry table expansion with wordline-aware interpolation and multi-dimensional guided retry.
workload_or_benchmark: 3D NAND retention experiments at 12 and 30 months; NAND generation, temperature, workload, page count, failure distribution, and baseline table are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 3D NAND flash with read-retry voltage reference combinations and wordline-dependent retention behavior; cell type, layers, controller, and ECC are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 99% usable capacity after 12 months
Up to 84% usable capacity after 30 months
limits: The description omits NAND generation, retention temperature, ECC contribution, failure count, retry latency, and capacity accounting.
Retention results may not generalize across vendors, workloads, temperatures, or wear levels.
Official description only; reliability and lifetime claims require paper-level verification.
